text:
mike: pushed a quick int6 smoke for newbreed-13b to the canary pool. cost delta looks promising (~2.3x token cost reduction vs fp16) but noticed quality drift on long-answer recall slices. sharing numbers below.

sarah: nailed the slices you flagged? which prompts/regimens caused the worst drift?

mike: mainly multi-step summarization and chain-of-thought style prompts where the model drops a clause or two. short answers are fine.

jia: uploaded the mini-scorecard to the drive: https://redwood.internal/sheets/small-scan-newbreed-int6  summary:
- longform recall: -1.7% exact-match (relative)
- rouge-lite: -0.9
- latency p95: +12ms
- per-1k-token cost: $0.048 (int6) vs $0.11 (fp16)

tom: p95 tail up is probably kv-cache cold start. did you run a warmstart / priming test?

mike: not yet. I can run a primed-vs-cold comparison. early theory: priming reduces repeated attention recompute, helps recall for multistep prompts.

jia: created a stratified sample to validate: 120 examples per slice (longform, multi-turn, rerank, single-shot). attached quick stats in doc.

emma-product: from GTN/product: our risk tolerance for recall regressions on longform is <=1.0% absolute. if it's >1% we need traffic split and canary with human-in-the-loop.

mike: current -1.7% (relative) maps to ~1.2% absolute for our primary evaluation set, so slightly over the threshold.

deploy-bot: deploy log: canary int6/newbreed-13b pushed to pool-qa at 2024-08-16T12:02:04Z. canary_id=cb-1740000000-a.

tom: proposal: hybrid routing + prefix-priming + selective int8 fallback for problem slices. idea: 85% int6, 10% int8 (fallback), 5% fp16 (investigate drift). use per-route score thresholds to escalate to higher-fidelity variants.

jia: ran a quick simulation for mixed fleet: weighted cost per 1k tokens -> (0.85*0.048 + 0.10*0.08 + 0.05*0.11) = $0.0536 approx. quality uplift on longform sim -> closes gap to 0.4% absolute. latency p95 slightly higher but within SLA.

emma-product: that looks promising. what about KV-cache priming? any numbers?

mike: priming test (seed 50 sessions):
```
primed: longform EM -0.3% vs fp16, p95 latency +6ms, effective tokens saved ~11% due to prefix reuse
cold: longform EM -1.7% vs fp16, p95 latency +12ms
```

jia: TL;DR: priming dramatically reduces the observed quality gap. combined with mixed-fleet fallback we can meet product gates.

tom: ops notes: need a rollout flag we can toggle by route. suggest flag: opt_quant_profile=newbreed-int6-hybrid-202408. Also need tracing hooks to verify fallback rate stays <15%.

mike: action plan I’ll run today:
1) priming benchmark across 3 slices (longform, multi-turn, rerank) -> detailed numbers posted.
2) simulate hybrid routing on live qps sample (24h) -> cost and fallback %
3) produce a one-page unit-econ sheet for GTN with recommended default.

emma-product: timeline ok: we need the unit-econ sheet before next product sync (48h). if numbers support, we’ll greenlight a limited canary in prod for low-risk routes.

jia: attaching quick snippet of the unit-econ calc we used for the simulation:
```
# simplified
cost_int6_per_1k = 0.048
cost_int8_per_1k = 0.08
cost_fp16_per_1k = 0.11
mix = {int6:0.85,int8:0.10,fp16:0.05}
expected_cost = sum(cost_*mix[*])
```

mike: note for the scorecard: include per-route "quality delta" and "fallback rate" plus cost-per-1k and p95 latency. product wants a single-row verdict: Accept / Hold / Rollout-with-constraints.

tom: ops constraint: fallback must be automated with circuit-breaker at 20% per-minute or we fail closed to fp16 to avoid bad UX.

emma-product: if priming + hybrid reduces absolute regression <=0.5% AND fallback <10% we can push to customer-facing canary for curated routes. otherwise, hold.

mike: I'll post the priming benchmarks and the one-page unit-econ in this thread when done. expect updates in ~6 hours. :thumbsup:

sarah: thanks — helpful. also add a quick note re: developer ergonomics (how to opt-in) and example config. small docs snippet will help solutions eng.

mike: will add. example config:
```
route: /generate/longform
quant_profile: newbreed-int6-hybrid-202408
fallback_policies:
  - threshold: quality_score < 0.85 -> int8
  - circuit_breaker: fallback_rate > 0.20 -> fp16
priming: true
priming_strategy: prefix-cache
```

jia: ping me if you want me to run additional significance tests on the sample. I can do bootstrapped CI for the EM diff.

mike: appreciated. will loop you in.

deploy-bot: canary metrics uploaded to dashboards at https://dashboards.internal/canaries/1740000000 (latency, fallback_rate, cost-per-1k).

emma-product: great. holding product sync decision pending your writeup. thanks everyone.
